idea: Graphics lives in a world of gaps. You have a few measurements—a handful of keyframes, some sparse pose estimates from cameras, a texture draped across a mesh, a handful of seed points—but you need a complete picture everywhere. The connective tissue is what fills those gaps: smooth blending between nearby known values, finding the closest matching pattern when you face something new, reshaping coordinates so relationships stay intact as you move from one frame or space to another, and tracking how pieces fit together (topology). This is not the flashy machinery of lighting and color; it is the quiet bookkeeping that lets every fancy technique work. The core realization is that the world does not jump: between two neighboring measurements, the truth stays close to their blend, and relationships—which pose is nearest, how a cloth drapes, which pixels influence which output pixels—survive honest rearrangement of space.
why: It works because smooth functions have no sudden cliffs. If you measure a surface at two nearby points and blend the values linearly (or with any smooth curve), you are extremely close to the real answer almost everywhere between them. Topological relationships—connectivity, ordering, which-is-nearest—do not depend on coordinates; a translation, rotation, or nonlinear warping changes where things sit but not how they relate. You can solve a hard problem in a convenient space (aligned pose space, latent coordinate space, flattened texture space) where relationships are simple, then carry the solution back to the original frame without breaking it. The catch is that this only holds for truly smooth underlying phenomena; if your data has cracks, isolated islands, or genuinely discontinuous transitions, blending and coordinate tricks hit a wall.
dots: The papers show this single move running through almost every problem. Blending pixels: Lucky High Dynamic Range learns to mix bracketed photos by training once and then applying the learned blend to new photos. Interpolation: LayerInbetween smoothly fills missing animation frames by tracking stroke strokes across layers and warping progressively. Manifold k-NN finds nearest neighbors by building a recursive hierarchy of spatial regions so you skip checking far-away points. Retargeting motion to a new character works by learning to adaptively adjust anchor points, then smoothly warping spatial relationships to fit the new body (Spatially Adaptive Interaction Guidance). Coordinate changes: PAColorHolo transforms distorted laser colors back to true colors via learned neural coordinate mappings. NeuBase preserves four sacred properties—linearity, locality, smoothness, and affine invariance—so neural deformations stay safe under coordinate changes. TwinPose reconstructs 3D pose from multiple 2D camera views by fitting poses into a learned person-specific subspace so each body stays within its natural movement patterns. MotionBricks compresses 350k motion clips into a learned latent space where similar poses cluster, then interpolates between motion primitives at runtime. The connecting thread: every approach assumes smoothness or learned distance structure, then uses blending, nearest-matching, or coordinate warping to carry information from known places to unknown ones.
picture: Imagine you have a few paint color swatches and need to fill a whole wall. You do not jump from swatch to swatch; you blend neighboring swatches to paint the in-between smoothly. Or imagine tracing a person's hand in a video where you see frames 1 and 5 clearly but frames 2, 3, 4 are blurry. You do not guess randomly; you smoothly warp where the hand was in frame 1 toward where it is in frame 5, interpolating the in-between positions. Or imagine moving a dance routine from one dancer's body to another's; you do not copy joint positions exactly (because bodies are different shapes), but you remember spatial relationships—which joints are near each other, which move together—and gently reshape those relationships to fit the new body. All of these are the same move: use what you know, blend smoothly to fill gaps, preserve the relationships that matter.
